title: End To End Testing Refactor
description: Implement the end-to-end testing refactor plan: make the nearest language-neutral domain owner the unit of test ownership. Deliver a new repo test domain (🧰️framework/🛍️products/🦑️repo/🔨️modules/🧪️test) owning taxonomy, Gherkin feature parsing, case discovery, scenario planning, oracle registry, native host protocols, result schemas, semantic comparison profiles, reporting, test-output cleanup and multi-ecosystem test dependency classification. Add Nx per-test-case project generation from **/🧪️tests/*/component.feature, native hosts for TypeScript/Rust/Go/Python/.NET, oracle-first development protocol, PDF pilots (pdf-writer creation oracle, lopdf editing oracle) on the ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio/🗿️artifacts/📄️pdf owner, safe `clean test`, taxonomy/testing policy breach families, multi-ecosystem dependency baseline with production reachability, CI gates, and launch.json entries. compose/** is a hard forbidden path for discovery, migration, cleaning, coverage and reports.
summary:
WAVE 5 — no CI workflow, and the open/closed rule is now enforced and measurably shrinking.

NO GITHUB ACTIONS. .github/workflows/test.yml deleted and unstaged. Every gate it ran is reachable as an Nx target and a launch entry instead: workspace:test-discover, test-doctor, test-contract, test-oracle, test-subject, test-parity, test-metrics, test-metrics-enforce, test-report, verify-layering, verify-layering-write-baseline, clean-test, clean-coverage.

THE FRAMEWORK NO LONGER DEPENDS ON s. 🧰️.../🧪️test/📇️registry/🔒️migration.json is deleted — it had listed six ✏️s owners by path. Per-owner migration status now lives with the owner in that owner's own 🧪️oracle/🔣️component.json and is collected by discovery; the repo-wide shrink-only ratchet moved to /🔒️migration.json beside 🔒️dependencies.json and is keyed by AREA, so a deleted area simply surveys as zero and passes; the os-kernel blocker prose moved to the ticket where it belongs. The framework test domain's four core sources now contain zero references to any implementation area, asserted by a self-test that reads `areaLayers` from the taxonomy and so names no area itself.

THE RULE IS ENFORCED, NOT ASSERTED. New taxonomy vocabulary (areaLayers, repoWideFiles, layeringGeneratedInventories, layeringGeneratedBanners) and a new domain-neutral library policy (layeringReferences, layeringCounts, layeringBreaches, writeLayeringBaseline) count every reference from repo-wide or framework code to an implementation area against a shrink-only baseline at /🔒️layering.json. Wired into `verify gate`, `workspace:verify-layering` and two launch entries. Four library self-tests hold the ratchet, including one that fails if a baselined file has already reached zero and should be dropped from the list.

THE NUMBER WENT DOWN: 930 authored references at first measurement → 465. Minus 123 for bundled build output (🟨️frame-worker.js), which regenerates itself and is detected by bundler banner so no artifact is listed by path. Minus 342 for POLICY_SEMANTIC_VOCABULARY_ALLOWLIST — 342 ✏️s paths that were sitting in the ROOT ROUTER. Those entries moved to ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🔒️policy-allowlist.json, owned by the area they describe, and the root rule now calls policyDiscoveredAllowlist(root, "semantic-vocabulary"), which merges every 🔒️policy-allowlist.json in the tree by convention — so deleting the area deletes its exemptions with it. Proven value-identical against HEAD (342 entries, identical set AND order) and proven actually consulted (596 vocabulary findings with the allowlist loaded, 567 with it emptied).

NOTHING REGRESSED: test-domain 52 pass / 0 fail / 703 assertions; repo-library 174 pass with 20 pre-existing failures (22 before this wave, all dependency-boundary / ui-css / playground-port churn from other sessions); contract 0 breaches; 24/24 oracle executions; 49/49 full-run executions with 37/37 parity; dependency ratchet clean; verify-layering clean.

WHAT IS LEFT, HONESTLY — 465 references in 45 files. 150 in the repo-CLI's own Go test (asserts on real monorepo contents; should assert against discovery), 138 in the root 📜️script.ts (about 18 leaf policy regions that are plugin-architecture rules and belong in ✏️s/🔌️plugins/📜️script.ts), 39 in the library's tests, 36 in the vscode extension test, 18 in the DSL fixture sweep, and 84 spread thinly over 40 further files. The 138 in the root router are the substantive remainder and need the shared policy toolkit (🔧️PolicyFsScan, ~219 lines) extracted into 📚️library first so an implementation's own 📜️script.ts can import it — the policy plugin already discovers such scripts, so once the toolkit is importable each rule moves as a unit. That extraction was deliberately NOT attempted here: the root script is being edited concurrently by another session and a half-finished toolkit move would leave the tree broken. The ratchet guarantees the count cannot rise while it waits.

Records: 📊️verification-wave5.txt.
